title: Arguing a position
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: geureoke + saenggakhal + su-do + isseoyo. + hajiman + clause

rules.text: THE PLAN GOES AT THE FRONT. cheotjjae, duljjae and majimageuro are not counting words: they tell a listener where in your case they have arrived. Say one, then the whole clause.
BECAUSE IS BRACKETED. waenyahamyeon opens the reason and -gi ttaemun-ieyo closes it. English says because once, at the join; Korean announces it at the front and finishes it at the end.
ONLY THE DISCOURSE WORDS FRONT. Every connective that joins two clauses sits at the END of the first one. A reason fronted with a bare ttaemun is a fragment, not a sentence.
-GI MAKES THE VERB A THING FIRST. eopseoyo becomes eopgi before ttaemun-ieyo can take it, the same move L4-M1 taught with hagi and gagi inside their own frames.

RAISE THE OBJECTION YOURSELF. geureoke saenggakhal su-do isseoyo names the other reading as thinkable; L1-M10's hajiman or L4-M4's geuraedo then turns it. L4-M4 conceded a point already made — here you invite one.
YEREUL DEUREO IS ONE PIECE. For example — never split it, and never bend deureo, which is not L4-M6's deureoyo, to enter.

THE FRAME IS DIRECT, THE SENTENCES ARE NOT. A case is argued in -yo, with L4-M5's softeners inside the clauses. Reaching for -(seu)pnida to sound authoritative is the register mistake this course spent two levels preventing.
FIVE NOUNS HOLD A CASE TOGETHER: jujang a claim, munje the problem, chanseong for, bandae against, gyeollon the conclusion.

words.note: The first item of a case, not the first thing in a queue. It opens the sentence and the whole clause follows it.

sentences.trap: English can drop first of all into the middle of a sentence. cheotjjae cannot move: it opens the sentence or it is not doing its job.

variations.cue: First, there was no time.
variations.changed: the past: the same frame over a finished reason

variations.cue: Second, there is no time.
variations.changed: the second slot of the same plan

mistake.why: The plan word cannot be an afterthought. cheotjjae exists to warn the listener that a list is starting, and a warning that arrives after the item is not a warning.

sentences.usage: Opening the first reason of a case.
sentences.mnemonic: cheot is first; cheotjjae is first place in your argument.

sentences.cue: Second, this restaurant is too expensive.

words.note: The second item, built the same way as cheotjjae. A case that opens with cheotjjae owes the listener a duljjae.

sentences.trap: duljjae counts your reasons, never the restaurants. For a second thing in the world Korean reaches for a counter, not for this word.

variations.cue: Second, this restaurant is too far.
variations.changed: a different second reason in the same slot

variations.cue: First, this restaurant is too expensive.
variations.changed: the same reason moved to the opening slot

mistake.why: Without the comma pause duljjae reads as counting restaurants — the second restaurant. The plan word stands alone before the clause begins.

sentences.usage: Adding the second reason, once the first has landed.
sentences.mnemonic: dul is two; duljjae is reason two.

words.note: It announces that a reason is coming and commits you to finishing with ttaemun-ieyo. Alone it is half a construction.
ttaemun is the reason itself and -ieyo is L1-M1's copula. It closes the bracket waenyahamyeon opened; L3-M3's ttaemune is the joining form, and is a different word here.

sentences.trap: English says because once and then runs on. Korean opens with waenyahamyeon and must still close with ttaemun-ieyo, so the reason is fenced at both ends.

variations.cue: It is because there is no time.
variations.changed: waenyahamyeon dropped: correct, but it no longer announces itself

variations.cue: Because I go to school.
variations.changed: L4-M1's gagi in the same bracket

mistake.why: The bracket was opened and never closed. A finished -yo verb cannot sit under waenyahamyeon: the clause has to end in -gi ttaemun-ieyo.

sentences.usage: Giving the reason behind a claim you have just made.
sentences.mnemonic: wae is why; waenyahamyeon is here comes the why.

sentences.cue: For example, the bus is too late.

words.note: Two words, one piece — raising an example. Learn it whole: deureo here is not L4-M6's deureoyo, to enter.

sentences.trap: English can put for example almost anywhere in a sentence. yereul deureo opens the example and nothing else goes in front of it.

variations.cue: For example, the train is too late.
variations.changed: a different example in the same frame

variations.cue: For example, the bus is too far.
variations.changed: the same subject, a different complaint

mistake.why: An example that announces itself after it has been given is not an example, it is a repetition. The frame goes first.

sentences.usage: Making an abstract reason concrete before an objection can.
sentences.mnemonic: ye is an example; yereul deureo raises one up.

sentences.display: Geureoke saenggakhal su-do isseoyo. Hajiman munje-ga isseoyo.
sentences.script: 그렇게 생각할 수도 있어요. 하지만 문제가 있어요.
sentences.cue: One could see it that way. But there is a problem.
sentences.literal: that-way think-FUT.ADN way-even exists. but problem-SUBJ exists

words.note: The form L3-M3's saenggakhaeyo takes in front of su. It is not a future: it only says the thinking has not happened yet.
L2-M1's su with L1-M3's -do attached. su isseoyo is one can; su-do isseoyo is one might well — which is what concedes the other side its reading.

sentences.trap: English concedes with a shrug — fair enough. Korean concedes by calling the other view thinkable, and the concession is worthless unless a turn follows it.
sentences.sound: GEU-reo-ke SAENG-ga-kal SU-do I-sseo-yo. HA-ji-man MUN-je-ga I-sseo-yo.

variations.display: Geureoke saenggakhal su-do isseoyo. Geuraedo munje-ga isseoyo.
variations.script: 그렇게 생각할 수도 있어요. 그래도 문제가 있어요.
variations.cue: One could see it that way. Even so, there is a problem.
variations.changed: L4-M4's geuraedo for hajiman: a softer turn

variations.cue: One could see it that way.
variations.changed: the concession alone, with the turn withheld

mistake.why: A finished verb cannot carry su. The verb has to become saenggakhal first, and only that form can hand the possibility to isseoyo.

sentences.usage: Naming the objection before your listener does.
sentences.mnemonic: su is the room to do it; su-do is even that much room.

sentences.display: Majimageuro, je gyeollon-eun ganeun geo-ga joayo.
sentences.script: 마지막으로, 제 결론은 가는 거가 좋아요.
sentences.cue: Lastly, my conclusion is that going is better.
sentences.literal: lastly, my conclusion-TOP go-ADN thing-SUBJ is-good

words.note: The close of a case, matching cheotjjae at the other end. It promises that nothing follows, so do not use it twice.
The finding a case arrives at. Said gyeol-lon: the two consonants at the seam assimilate, and the romanization writes what is said.

sentences.trap: English can say finally and then keep talking for a minute. majimageuro is a promise that the next sentence ends the case.
sentences.sound: MA-ji-ma-geu-ro, je GYEOL-lo-neun GA-neun GEO-ga JO-a-yo.

variations.cue: Lastly, I will state my conclusion.
variations.changed: -eul for -eun: the conclusion as the thing said

variations.cue: My conclusion is that going is better.
variations.changed: the close dropped: a conclusion with no announcement

mistake.why: A conclusion is a thing, so what follows it has to be a thing too. L5-M5's ganeun geo-ga does that work; a bare finished verb leaves gyeollon-eun with nothing to be.

sentences.usage: Closing a case with the finding it was built for.
sentences.mnemonic: majimak is the last one; majimageuro is by way of the last one.

sentences.display: Chingu-neun chanseong-ieyo. Hajiman je jujang-eun dallayo.
sentences.script: 친구는 찬성이에요. 하지만 제 주장은 달라요.
sentences.cue: My friend is for it. But my claim is different.
sentences.literal: friend-TOP agreement-is. but my claim-TOP differs

words.note: A noun, not a verb: Korean says a person IS agreement rather than that they agree. Its opposite is bandae.
What you are arguing, held apart from whether it is true. A case has one jujang and several reasons under it.

sentences.trap: English makes these verbs — he agrees, I argue. Korean keeps them nouns and lets the copula or dallayo do the work, so nothing is conjugated at all.
sentences.sound: CHIN-gu-neun CHAN-seong-i-e-yo. HA-ji-man je JU-jang-eun DAL-la-yo.

variations.display: Chingu-neun bandae-yeyo. Hajiman je jujang-eun dallayo.
variations.script: 친구는 반대예요. 하지만 제 주장은 달라요.
variations.cue: My friend is against it. But my claim is different.
variations.changed: bandae for chanseong: the other side of the same frame

variations.display: Chingu-neun chanseong-ieyo. Geuraedo je jujang-eun dallayo.
variations.script: 친구는 찬성이에요. 그래도 제 주장은 달라요.
variations.cue: My friend is for it. Even so, my claim is different.
variations.changed: geuraedo for hajiman: the turn made gentler

mistake.why: The verb exists, but at this level the noun with the copula is what a case is built from — and it is the shape that lets chanseong and bandae stand side by side in one sentence.

sentences.usage: Placing yourself against a position somebody else holds.
sentences.mnemonic: chanseong sides with; jujang is the side you take.

sentences.display: Munje-ga hana isseoyo. Sigan-i neomu jjalbayo.
sentences.script: 문제가 하나 있어요. 시간이 너무 짧아요.
sentences.cue: There is one problem. The time is too short.
sentences.literal: problem-SUBJ one exists. time-SUBJ too is-short

words.note: The thing wrong with a position — yours or theirs. Naming one munje and answering it is worth more than listing five.

sentences.trap: English says there is a problem with that, and the with-phrase carries the target. Korean names the problem and then states it as a separate sentence, which is why a case reads as short steps.
sentences.sound: MUN-je-ga HA-na I-sseo-yo. SI-ga-ni NEO-mu JJAL-ba-yo.

variations.display: Munje-ga manhi isseoyo. Sigan-i neomu jjalbayo.
variations.script: 문제가 많이 있어요. 시간이 너무 짧아요.
variations.cue: There are many problems. The time is too short.
variations.changed: manhi for hana: a pile of them instead of one

variations.cue: There is no problem.
variations.changed: the negative: the objection refused outright

mistake.why: The count follows the noun it counts. Korean says problem-one-exists, and a number fronted onto the noun reads as English word order in Korean words.

sentences.usage: Naming the single weak point you intend to press.
sentences.mnemonic: munje is the question put to your case.

sentences.display: Waenyahamyeon jeo-neun jigeum sigan-i eopgi ttaemun-ieyo.
sentences.script: 왜냐하면 저는 지금 시간이 없기 때문이에요.
sentences.cue: Because right now I have no time.
sentences.literal: because I-TOP now time-SUBJ not-existing reason-is

words.note: eopseoyo turned into a thing so ttaemun can take it, exactly as L4-M1 turns hada into hagi. Said eop-gi, with the p.

sentences.trap: English keeps the verb a verb inside because. Korean has to nominalise it first, so the clause under waenyahamyeon never ends in -yo.
sentences.sound: WAE-nya-ha-myeon JEO-neun JI-geum SI-ga-ni EOP-gi TTAE-mu-ni-e-yo.

variations.display: Waenyahamyeon jeo-neun jigeum hakgyo-e gagi ttaemun-ieyo.
variations.script: 왜냐하면 저는 지금 학교에 가기 때문이에요.
variations.cue: Because I am going to school right now.
variations.changed: gagi for eopgi: the same slot, a motion verb

variations.cue: I have no time right now.
variations.changed: the bracket removed: a plain statement, not a reason

mistake.display: Waenyahamyeon jeo-neun jigeum sigan-i eopseoyo ttaemun-ieyo.
mistake.script: 왜냐하면 저는 지금 시간이 없어요 때문이에요.
mistake.why: ttaemun needs a noun in front of it, and a finished -yo verb is not one. eopseoyo has to become eopgi before the bracket can close.

sentences.usage: Backing a refusal you have already softened.
sentences.mnemonic: eopseoyo loses its ending and becomes eopgi, a thing you can point at.

sentences.display: Je jujang-eun chanseong-ieyo. Hajiman bandae-do manhi isseoyo.
sentences.script: 제 주장은 찬성이에요. 하지만 반대도 많이 있어요.
sentences.cue: My position is yes. But there is a lot of opposition too.
sentences.literal: my claim-TOP agreement-is. but opposition-even much exists

words.note: chanseong's opposite, and a noun in the same way. bandae-yeyo is I am against it; bandae-do adds L1-M3's -do, opposition as well.

sentences.trap: English hears I am against as a stance. Korean bandae-yeyo is nearer to my answer is no, so it reports a position rather than a feeling and is far less confrontational than it looks.
sentences.sound: je JU-jang-eun CHAN-seong-i-e-yo. HA-ji-man BAN-dae-do MA-ni I-sseo-yo.

variations.display: Je jujang-eun chanseong-ieyo. Geuraedo bandae-do manhi isseoyo.
variations.script: 제 주장은 찬성이에요. 그래도 반대도 많이 있어요.
variations.cue: My position is yes. Even so, there is a lot of opposition too.
variations.changed: geuraedo for hajiman: conceding the count without conceding the case

variations.cue: My position is no.
variations.changed: the position reversed and the objection dropped

mistake.display: Je jujang-eun chanseong-ieyo. Hajiman bandae manhi isseoyo.
mistake.script: 제 주장은 찬성이에요. 하지만 반대 많이 있어요.
mistake.why: Dropping -do loses the whole point of the sentence. Without it the second clause merely reports opposition; with it, the opposition is granted as well as reported.

sentences.usage: Granting how much stands against you without moving.
sentences.mnemonic: bandae turns back against; chanseong stands with.

comprehensionPool.cue: For example, the bus is late.
One could see it that way.
Lastly, I will state my conclusion.
But the time is too short.
Even so, I think going is better.
